item.title: ICE agent in New York shooting also involved in assault of pregnant woman
item.description:
The ICE shooting of a 28-year-old in the Bronx Thursday has provoked an uproar among New Yorkers, who rushed to the streets in protest the night of the shooting, clashing with the New York Police Department. At least five protesters were arrested. And though members of the NYPD were not involved in the shooting, they were involved in arresting protesters and, some witnesses say, protecting ICE vehicles—despite a New York State law that prohibits local police departments from collaborating with the federal agency, as well as local “sanctuary city” laws. Allies of Mayor Zohran Mamdani are now calling on his police commissioner, Jessica Tisch, to step down if ICE does not leave New York City. item.title: Candidate named Hitler Mussolini elected mayor in Peru
item.description:
A politician named Hitler Mussolini Simeón Flores has won a mayoral election in Peru, securing 229 votes on a center-left party ticket. Simeón, 45, finished first in Queropalca, a district in Peru’s Huánuco region with a population of just over 730 people. Running for the Ahora Nación (Now Nation) party, he received 34.5% of the 663 valid votes cast in the election. His nearest competitor, Gaspar Benilde Osorio Zambrano of Popular Renewal Peru, received 204 votes, putting Simeón ahead by 25. His victory awaits formal proclamation by the electoral authority. Simeón’s name evokes Adolf Hitler, the leader of Nazi Germany, and Benito Mussolini, Italy’s fascist dictator and Hitler’s wartime ally. According to his candidate declaration, Simeón resigned from the populist right-wing Popular Force party in 2025 before running for Ahora Nación. item.title: ‘Digger’ has a lot of haters. Here’s why they’re wrong.
item.description:
Last week, this magazine published a review of Digger , the new climate change allegory from Mexican provocateur Alejandro Iñárritu. In it, my colleague Jake Bittle explains in detail why he “ hated it .” I was skeptical of the bad reviews that Digger has been getting; after all, I like more of the Iñárritu films I’ve seen than not. I would even call one of them (his 2001 debut, Amores Perros ) a cinematic masterpiece. ( Birdman was fine.) In any case, most of the time a Mexican person is in the news, I am invested in their success, so I decided to see the movie for myself. Even then — two hours, nine minutes, and a small popcorn later — I was surprised by my reaction: I simply loved the movie. item.title: Unpacking the Environmental Issues in Susan Collins’ Tough Race in Maine
item.description:
BATH, Maine — Election after election, Republican Sen. Susan Collins has defied national political winds to return to office, representing a state that has backed Democrats in every presidential contest since 1992. But her Democratic opponent, Troy Jackson, is betting that her eight-year-old vote to confirm Justice Brett Kavanaugh and the Supreme Court’s subsequent overturning of federal abortion rights will persuade voters to sweep her out of office. item.title: What the Iran war has done to the world’s energy supply, in charts
item.description:
In the immediate aftermath of the 9/11 attacks, a vengeful America was braying for blood. Nine out of 10 Americans approved of attacking Afghanistan. About one-third were comfortable with the prospect of Afghan civilian deaths . Less than a quarter thought the conflict would last more than two years. Hardy bands of protesters took to the streets in New York City, D.C., and elsewhere in a vain attempt to prevent the war. They were called scum and traitors and worse. Americans got the war that most of them wanted — and it was an abject disaster . The invasion of Afghanistan begat conflicts across the world: a sprawling global war that brought death and destruction to Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Iran, Iraq, Libya, Niger, the Philippines, Somalia, Syria, Tunisia, Venezuela, and Yemen, among other locales.
